# Theama — complete setup guide

Start with your own media folders and a video player. Add online features only when you want them. You can skip any wizard step, finish later, and return to Settings → Setup Guide. Instructions are bundled with the app and remain readable offline; downloads, registration, and online tests need an internet connection.

<a id="welcome"></a>

## Before you start: apps, accounts, and keys

Theama has no account of its own. A local library needs no third-party API key. The table explains exactly what each feature needs.

| Feature | Install or register | Credential entered in Theama | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local library | Theama and accessible media folders | None | Settings → Library |
| Packaged backend | Windows service; runtime, NSSM and FFprobe are bundled | Windows account password in the service credential dialog, if requested | Service step / Advanced → Service |
| Video playback | One video player, or an existing Windows file association | None | Settings → Playback |
| Posters and identification (optional) | TMDB account and API registration | TMDB v3 API key OR API Read Access Token | Settings → Metadata |
| Subtitle downloads (optional) | OpenSubtitles.com and/or SubDL account | A separate API key for each provider; OpenSubtitles login is optional | Settings → Playback → Subtitle providers |
| Downloads (optional) | qBittorrent with Web UI enabled | Web UI URL, username, password; no API key | Settings → Downloads |
| Indexer search (optional) | Prowlarr and your chosen indexers | Prowlarr URL and API key | Settings → Downloads |
| VPN status (optional) | NordVPN Windows app and account | None; sign in inside NordVPN | Downloads tool panel |
| Source builds only | Git, Node.js, repository-pinned Yarn | None for development; signing certificate only for signed installers | Developer appendix |

Theama generates its local API bearer token automatically in the data folder. It is not a TMDB or subtitle key and should not be pasted into provider fields. The current integrations require no IMDb, YouTube, or Wikidata API key. Never put real keys in source code, screenshots, issue reports, or this guide.

Choose English or Ελληνικά in the wizard. Metadata language and preferred subtitle languages are separate settings: changing the interface language does not translate an existing filename or choose a subtitle provider.

<a id="installation"></a>

## Install Theama on Windows

Use a trusted Windows x64 installer supplied by the project, or build the installer from this repository. A public release download is not currently confirmed.

1. If you have a project-supplied Theama-Setup-&lt;version&gt;.exe, close the old app and run it. Follow the installer’s prompts and approve its elevation request when appropriate. Do not download a similarly named application from an unrelated site.
2. The installer includes Electron, the backend’s Node.js runtime, the database module, NSSM, and FFprobe. Installed-app users do not need Git, Yarn, Python, a separate database server, or a manual FFmpeg installation for the basic library.
3. Launch Theama from the installed shortcut. The installer does not create the Windows service on first install: use the wizard’s Backend step or the recovery screen to install it with your chosen account.
4. Once the backend is connected, add one small media folder and select a player. Check that a file appears and plays before importing all your drives.
5. If no installer was supplied, use the Developer appendix. The repository Releases page was unavailable during preparation of this guide; this guide does not promise a downloadable published build.

- [Project repository and source](https://github.com/tasoskour/theama)

<a id="service"></a>

## Backend and Windows service

The normal packaged app connects to a background Windows service. Development runs the backend as a normal process without service installation.

1. In the wizard’s Backend step, choose Install if the service is not installed. The same action is on the recovery screen and Settings → Advanced → Service.
2. Choose your current Windows account for access to that account’s media, or Local System for local folders it can access. Approve the Windows UAC prompt. For your account, enter its actual account password if the credential dialog asks; a Windows Hello PIN is not that password. Never type your Windows password into a metadata or download form.
3. Wait for the service to start and the connection indicator to say Connected. If it is installed but stopped, use Start. Start, Stop and Restart ordinarily need no further elevation after installation grants control permissions.
4. Check that the service account can read your media. Download destinations and subtitle folders also need write permission. For network shares, use a UNC path such as \\\\NAS\\Media\\Movies and an account permitted by the share; desktop-mapped drive letters may not exist in the service session.
5. Use Repair after installation-path or account problems. Install, Repair and Uninstall can request elevation. Uninstalling the service leaves the library data. Closing the app does not normally stop the installed service.

If the backend is unavailable, the guide and this step remain usable. Other forms requiring the backend are disabled until it connects. Cancelling UAC or the credential dialog leaves setup incomplete; retry when ready. In yarn dev, do not install a service: the development process controller starts the backend itself.

- [NSSM project information (bundled in installers)](https://nssm.cc/download)

<a id="library"></a>

## Add and scan media folders

Add the folders that actually contain your video files. A folder can contain movies, series, personal videos, or a mixture classified automatically.

1. Choose Add folder in this step or Settings → Library. Browse to a folder such as D:\\Media\\Movies, D:\\Media\\Series, or E:\\Family Videos.
2. Choose Movies, Series, My Videos, or Automatic. Use My Videos for personal recordings that should not be identified as commercial films. Keep recursive scanning enabled when media sits in subfolders.
3. Let the first scan finish. The watcher scans later changes and rechecks returning drives. A saved folder counts as configured even if its scan is still running; an offline folder needs attention.
4. For better identification, include the title and year in movie names, for example Interstellar (2014)\\Interstellar (2014).mkv. For series, include S01E01, for example Severance\\Season 01\\Severance.S01E01.mkv.
5. Use folder exclusions for samples, extras or unwanted directories. If a drive letter changes, relocate the existing source instead of adding it again. Disconnecting a drive keeps its titles in the library, marked Offline; it does not mean the records were deleted.
6. Open a title and verify the file path. Check duration, resolution and codecs after probing completes. If absent, see Missing media details in troubleshooting. Add your other folders after this initial verification.

Choose download destinations from these same library sources later. Avoid unnecessary overlapping sources. The Windows service needs access to the real paths, even when Explorer can already browse them under your desktop account.

<a id="playback"></a>

## Install and choose a video player

VLC is a straightforward starting choice. MPC-HC, MPC-BE and mpv also support position tracking. PotPlayer, custom programs and the Windows default remain usable with limitations.

- [VLC for Windows — VideoLAN](https://www.videolan.org/vlc/download-windows.html)
- [MPC-HC — maintained clsid2 releases](https://github.com/clsid2/mpc-hc/releases)
- [MPC-BE releases](https://github.com/Aleksoid1978/MPC-BE/releases)
- [mpv installation and Windows build options](https://mpv.io/installation/)
- [PotPlayer official site](https://potplayer.daum.net/)

1. Install one player from its official page. Choose a normal Windows x64 installer when available. mpv’s installation page lists Windows packages, including third-party builds; follow the chosen package’s instructions.
2. Return to this step or Settings → Playback and choose Rescan. Theama checks known installation folders and PATH. Select the available player as the default.
3. For a portable or nonstandard installation, choose Add program and browse to the player’s .exe. Adding it as a custom program allows launching it but does not automatically give it the built-in integration’s tracking capabilities.
4. Open a local movie and press Play. Close and reopen it after watching briefly to check resume with a tracked player. Media on an offline drive cannot be played until the drive returns.
5. Choose your preferred subtitle languages in order, for example Greek then English. Existing subtitle files beside a video are discovered automatically. Use language suffixes such as Movie.el.srt and Movie.en.srt.
6. Review automatic next episode and countdown settings. These apply to supported tracked players; manual watched marking is still available.

VLC, mpv, MPC-HC and MPC-BE can report playback position through their supported local interfaces. Theama configures those interfaces when launching them; you do not need to publish a player web interface yourself. PotPlayer and custom/system players do not supply tracked progress. PotPlayer is launched on the video only; automatic external subtitle selection is not supported by its integration. A Windows default association is a fallback, not proof that a suitable player is installed.

<a id="metadata"></a>

## TMDB: posters, identification and descriptions

Optional. Without TMDB, scanning and local playback still work. With it, Theama can identify movies/series and fetch artwork, cast, summaries and episode information.

- [Create a TMDB account](https://www.themoviedb.org/signup)
- [TMDB account → API](https://www.themoviedb.org/settings/api)
- [Official API registration instructions](https://developer.themoviedb.org/docs/getting-started)

1. Create a TMDB account in a desktop browser and complete its email-verification process. Sign in, open your account settings, then API.
2. Follow the current API application flow. Choose the option appropriate for your actual personal use and accept the provider’s terms. Describe Theama honestly as your personal desktop media library; use the project repository as the project reference where applicable. Do not invent a published website or commercial approval.
3. Copy either the API Key (v3 auth), normally a 32-character hexadecimal value, or the API Read Access Token. The read token is longer and contains dot-separated parts. Both are supported; copy only the value, without quotation marks or a Bearer prefix.
4. In this step or Settings → Metadata, paste it into the TMDB key/token field and choose Save. Theama checks new credentials before keeping them. A rejection stays on the form; correct the value rather than proceeding as if it worked.
5. Choose metadata language separately from interface language. Watch the state and matched/ambiguous/unmatched/pending counts while background matching runs.
6. Open an identified title and verify its poster, year and summary. When a result is ambiguous, choose the correct match; user-confirmed choices are locked. Use the title’s matching controls to correct a wrong identification.
7. Use Replace to rotate the key, Remove to disconnect, and Retry after temporary network/provider failures. Existing cached information remains useful offline, but new metadata requests need the provider.

An Idle or Working state with a configured key indicates the metadata workflow is ready. Invalid key and Unavailable need attention. A key saved in the past does not guarantee current network access. Provider access rules and limits can change; check the official pages rather than relying on a fixed quota.

<a id="subtitles"></a>

## OpenSubtitles and SubDL

Optional. Configure either provider or both. Local subtitles already next to videos require no API key. Online downloads are initiated manually.

- [OpenSubtitles.com — API consumers and keys](https://www.opensubtitles.com/en/consumers)
- [SubDL — account API-key panel](https://subdl.com/panel/api)
- [SubDL — search/download API documentation](https://subdl.com/api-doc)

1. OpenSubtitles: register or sign in at OpenSubtitles.com, verify the account if requested, and open the API consumers page linked above. Create/register an API consumer using truthful application details, follow the displayed terms and copy its API key. This is the .com service; credentials for an older .org account may differ.
2. In this step or Settings → Playback → Subtitle providers, paste the key in the OpenSubtitles API-key field and choose Save. Use Test to check the configured provider. If you want account-based access, enter your OpenSubtitles username and password in its separate login form after saving the key. The account login does not replace the API key.
3. SubDL: create/sign in to your SubDL account, open the API panel, obtain a key, and paste it into the SubDL API-key field. Save, then Test. Theama currently uses SubDL API v1; its API documentation describes that endpoint even if newer API products are also advertised.
4. Choose subtitle languages in Playback, in preference order. In a movie’s file details or an expanded episode, choose Find subtitles, language and provider, then Search. Choose a matching release and download.
5. If an archive contains several subtitle files, select the desired entry. Theama validates SRT, ASS, SSA or VTT content and saves it beside the video without replacing an existing file. The service account needs write permission there. Play again to discover the saved subtitle.
6. Replace or remove each provider key independently. Log out of OpenSubtitles to remove the optional account login. Re-enter provider secrets after moving to a new data folder or restoring a database onto another machine.

Each provider applies its own request/download allowances, account rules and possible paid tiers. Check your account’s current usage and the provider’s official terms. A quota error does not mean the video is damaged. Tests verify provider access; they do not promise that a subtitle exists for every release. API credentials are stored locally in secrets/subtitles.json and are excluded from database backups.

<a id="downloads"></a>

## qBittorrent: connect the download client

Optional. qBittorrent performs downloads; Theama submits selected releases and monitors them. The connection needs a Web UI login, not an API key.

- [qBittorrent official downloads](https://www.qbittorrent.org/download)
- [qBittorrent options and Web UI documentation](https://github.com/qbittorrent/qBittorrent/wiki/Explanation-of-Options-in-qBittorrent)

1. Install qBittorrent for Windows and start it. Open Tools → Options → Web UI, enable the Web User Interface (Remote control), and note its HTTP port. For this-PC setup, use a local address and keep access local. Put the port shown there into the address; 8080 is only the usual default, for example http://localhost:8080.
2. Set the Web UI username and a strong password, then apply the changes. If your qBittorrent version generates a temporary password, follow its startup/log instructions to sign in and set your own password. Do not assume adminadmin is valid.
3. Open the configured Web UI address in your browser and verify that the same username/password logs in. Keep authentication and the normal host/CSRF protections enabled; do not disable them to work around a typo.
4. In this step or Settings → Downloads, enter Address, Username and Password under qBittorrent, then Connect. Use the full http:// or https:// URL, not the BitTorrent peer port. A configured but closed client is shown as unreachable; a rejected login must be corrected.
5. Choose movie and series destination folders from sources already added to Library. Leaving a destination at its default lets qBittorrent choose its own save folder, which may be outside your library. Ensure qBittorrent can write the destination and Theama’s service can read it.
6. Configure a release-search source using the next section. Find a download on a title, choose a release you are permitted to obtain, then check its progress on Downloads. For a magnet, file selection becomes available after qBittorrent fetches metadata.
7. By default Theama lists/manages torrents tagged by Theama. Show all my qBittorrent torrents deliberately expands that view and the available management actions. Completion-triggered library scans apply to Theama-added downloads with known library destinations.
8. Use Edit to change URL/login or Remove to forget the connection. Those actions do not uninstall qBittorrent. Pause, resume, file selection and removal are separate download actions; read any file-deletion confirmation carefully.

If qBittorrent runs on another machine, localhost refers to the backend’s machine, not that remote computer. Use an address reachable by the service and ensure save paths mean the same location to both programs. Theama does not implement remote-path translation. Do not expose these local interfaces publicly as part of setup.

<a id="prowlarr"></a>

## Release search: Prowlarr

Prowlarr finds releases through your chosen indexers. qBittorrent downloads the release you select. Theama ships no indexers or search plugins.

- [Prowlarr official Windows installer](https://prowlarr.com/#download)
- [Prowlarr quick start](https://wiki.servarr.com/prowlarr/quick-start-guide)

1. For Prowlarr, download its Windows x64 installer, follow the installer prompts and start it. Open its local interface, normally http://localhost:9696. Complete the initial authentication setup required by your version and save your chosen login.
2. In Prowlarr → Indexers, add an indexer you are entitled to use. Provide any credentials it requires, Test, then Save. Run a search inside Prowlarr before connecting Theama; an empty manager cannot supply releases.
3. Open Prowlarr → Settings → General; enable advanced settings if necessary and find Security → API Key. Copy that API key, not your browser-session password or an individual indexer’s key.
4. In Theama → Settings → Downloads → Prowlarr, enter its base Address (normally http://localhost:9696) and API key, then Connect. Configure qBittorrent separately above: a Prowlarr connection alone cannot download a file. Adding Theama as a Sonarr/Radarr application in Prowlarr is not required for this direct integration.
5. Search from a title in Theama. Prowlarr must be configured for release search. If it is unreachable, check its address, API key, and enabled indexers.
6. If results appear but the download cannot start, ensure qBittorrent can reach any torrent URL generated by Prowlarr. A localhost address produced on one machine can be wrong from another machine. Change keys with Edit; Remove disconnects the provider.

Provider/indexer access, accounts and restrictions are managed in Prowlarr. Only download material you have permission to obtain.

<a id="vpn"></a>

## Optional NordVPN app and status

Theama can open NordVPN and display its connection checks. A VPN subscription is optional and no NordVPN key or password is entered into Theama.

- [NordVPN official Windows download](https://nordvpn.com/download/windows/)

1. If you want this integration, install NordVPN for Windows and sign in inside NordVPN with your own account. Any subscription or account requirements belong to NordVPN.
2. Choose a location and connect in NordVPN. Return to Downloads or Downloads settings and refresh the tools/status panel. Open NordVPN opens a detected installation; it does not install the program or sign in for you.
3. Treat Connected as a verified check at that moment, Disconnected as no active supported tunnel, and Unknown as not verified. Running the NordVPN process alone does not prove a protected route. Checks can be stale, fail, or be unable to recognize a tunnel.
4. If Unknown persists, verify the connection inside NordVPN, check split tunnelling and routing, then refresh. The status panel provides information; it is not a kill switch and does not itself prevent downloads.

<a id="maintenance"></a>

## Data, secrets, backups and updates

Keep your library history safe and know which data a database backup contains. Installed and development instances normally use different data directories.

| Location | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| %ProgramData%\Theama | Normal installed-app data directory; an override can change it |
| .dev-data in the repository | Normal yarn dev data directory |
| data\theama.db | Library database, relative to the data directory |
| secrets\api-token | Generated local API token |
| secrets\tmdb.key | TMDB key/token |
| secrets\subtitles.json | Subtitle-provider keys and optional OpenSubtitles credentials |
| secrets\qbittorrent.json and secrets\prowlarr.json | Download-client login and indexer API key |
| backups, restore, logs, cache | Database copies, staged restore, diagnostics logs and replaceable cached artwork |

1. Open Settings → Advanced → About to inspect the actual data paths and versions. Use its folder buttons when needed. A configured THEAMA_DATA_DIR overrides the normal location.
2. In Settings → Advanced → Backups, create a backup before risky library changes. The app also makes daily and pre-upgrade backups. Keep an additional copy outside the machine when appropriate.
3. Database backups contain library records, watched history, matches and saved database settings. They do not include your video files, cached artwork, provider secrets, or desktop/profile preferences such as the wizard’s progress and player preferences. Store any needed secrets separately and securely.
4. Choose a backup to restore or select an external backup, review the confirmation, then restart the backend when requested. A staged restore is applied on startup, not immediately over the open database. The current database is backed up before replacement.
5. After restoring on a new machine, add/recover provider secrets, check player installation and paths, and verify media-folder permissions. Source identifiers in the database cannot make a missing drive available.
6. Update by running a newer trusted installer. Automatic updating is not established by this setup work. Use Settings → Advanced → Logs for recent errors and About → Copy diagnostics report for support. Review the report’s file paths before sharing; never attach the secrets folder.

Setup progress is local to the app/browser profile. Restart setup resets only its step history and skips, not your folders, keys, connections, or watched records. If profile storage is unavailable, setup remains usable for the current session but may not remember progress next launch.

<a id="developer"></a>

## Developer appendix: source, configuration and packaging

Use this section when running or building from source. Ordinary installed-app users can skip it.

- [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/downloads/win)
- [Node.js downloads](https://nodejs.org/en/download)
- [Yarn installation](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install)
- [FFmpeg/FFprobe build source](https://www.gyan.dev/ffmpeg/builds/)
- [NSSM downloads](https://nssm.cc/download)

1. Install Git for Windows and Node.js ≥22; Node 24 is the repository-tested default. Reopen PowerShell and check git --version and node --version. You need repository access to clone it.
2. The repository pins Yarn 4.18.1 and includes its release file. The commands below invoke that file directly, avoiding a global Yarn/Corepack requirement. If you prefer the yarn command, configure Corepack or an existing Yarn installation without changing the repository’s pinned version.
3. Clone the repository, enter its directory, install dependencies, fetch checksum-verified FFprobe, and start development. Do not run service installation just to develop the UI.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/tasoskour/theama.git
Set-Location theama
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs install
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs ffprobe:fetch
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs dev
```

The shorter commands below assume yarn resolves to the pinned repository release. yarn dev starts Vite at http://localhost:5173 and Electron, whose development controller starts the backend in .dev-data. It handles ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE exported by editor shells. The backend’s default port is 47890; another instance can cause a conflict.

```powershell
yarn typecheck
yarn lint
yarn test
yarn test:e2e
yarn build
yarn docs:setup --check
```

1. For an unsigned Windows installer, fetch NSSM and refresh FFprobe with its license files, then run dist. The generated artifact is build/installer/Theama-Setup-&lt;version&gt;.exe. Build on Windows x64; the staging step packages the Node executable used for the build.
2. Use yarn pack:dir for the unpacked application or yarn test:packaged for its smoke test. These are build outputs, not published releases.
3. To install the actual service from source, build first, fetch NSSM and FFprobe, then run yarn service:install. It requests elevation and normally uses your account; append --system for Local System. service:repair and service:uninstall provide the corresponding maintenance actions. Keep development and service data paths distinct.

```powershell
yarn nssm:fetch
yarn ffprobe:fetch --force
yarn dist
```

For signed packaging only, supply your own valid code-signing certificate using CSC_LINK and its password using CSC_KEY_PASSWORD through your local environment or CI secret store, then run yarn dist:signed. yarn verify:signature checks the output. No signing certificate is required to develop or make an unsigned local installer.

| Environment variable | Use and default |
| --- | --- |
| THEAMA_DATA_DIR | Override the backend data directory; desktop and backend must use the same directory |
| THEAMA_PORT | Backend port, normally 47890; 0 requests an available port |
| THEAMA_HOST_MODE | foreground or service; normally selected by the launcher/controller |
| THEAMA_LOG_LEVEL | trace, debug, info, warn, error; explicit environment setting overrides saved log detail |
| THEAMA_FFPROBE | Full ffprobe.exe path; none disables probing |
| THEAMA_EXTRA_ORIGINS | Comma-separated extra browser origins; needed for a separate browser dev server |
| THEAMA_TMDB_API_BASE / THEAMA_TMDB_IMAGE_BASE | Testing or mirror endpoints; normally official TMDB services |
| THEAMA_WIKIDATA_ENDPOINT | Optional alternate SPARQL endpoint |
| THEAMA_OPENSUBTITLES_API_BASE | Optional test/mirror API endpoint |
| THEAMA_SUBDL_API_BASE / THEAMA_SUBDL_DOWNLOAD_BASE | Optional test/mirror endpoints |
| THEAMA_CONTROLLER | dev when unpackaged; nssm when packaged. process is for packaged smoke testing |
| VITE_API_BASE / VITE_API_TOKEN | Plain-browser development only; Electron injects its local token itself |

Set variables in PowerShell before starting the process. This app does not automatically load a .env file. Keep provider keys in their Settings forms, not environment examples. For browser-only development, obtain the generated api-token locally, set VITE_API_TOKEN privately, allow the browser origin, and restart Vite after changing VITE variables. A direct browser health request without the local token is rejected by design.

```powershell
$env:THEAMA_DATA_DIR = Join-Path $PWD '.dev-data-custom'
$env:THEAMA_PORT = '47891'
$env:THEAMA_LOG_LEVEL = 'debug'
$env:THEAMA_EXTRA_ORIGINS = 'http://localhost:5173'
yarn dev
# In a later session, remove a temporary override:
Remove-Item Env:THEAMA_LOG_LEVEL -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

<a id="troubleshooting"></a>

## Troubleshooting by symptom

Start with the failing feature’s own status. Check the external application or account before changing Theama’s configuration.

### Backend not connected / service will not install

Open the Backend step or recovery screen. Check installed/stopped state, retry Start, inspect local logs, and verify the account password and UAC result. Do not confuse a Windows PIN with the password. If development is already using port 47890, stop that instance or give it a different data directory and port.

### Invalid TMDB or subtitle key

Copy a fresh complete value from the correct provider account. Remove quotes, spaces at the edges, and any Bearer prefix. Do not interchange keys between TMDB, OpenSubtitles, SubDL and Prowlarr. Replace the rejected value and use the available Save/Test action; optional OpenSubtitles login still requires its API key.

### qBittorrent or Prowlarr unreachable / incorrect port

Start the external program. Open its configured address in a browser on the backend machine. Confirm protocol, host, port, Web UI enablement and any URL base. localhost is the machine making the request. Check firewall/VPN local-access rules without disabling authentication.

### Web UI login rejected or forbidden

Verify qBittorrent Web UI credentials in a browser. Use the Web UI password rather than a Windows or Prowlarr password. Correct the host/address configuration and wait for any failed-login ban to expire before retrying repeatedly. Consult the official Web UI options for your version.

### No releases found

Search in Prowlarr first. It needs a working enabled indexer. Check title, year or season, and Theama’s unmatched-results control. If Prowlarr is unreachable, check its address and API key.

### Player missing or Play fails

Install a supported Windows player, Rescan, then select it. For a portable path, Add program and choose its executable. Verify the file still exists and the drive is online. Custom/system players may launch without resume tracking; choose a built-in tracked integration when progress is needed.

### Folder offline or access denied

Reconnect the drive, check its letter, and use source relocation if it changed. Verify read permission under the service account; download and subtitle destinations need write permission. Use an accessible UNC path for shares instead of assuming your desktop’s mapped drive exists in a service.

### Subtitle quota reached, no matches, or download fails

Check provider account usage and retry when its allowance resets. Try another configured provider or a more accurate release/language. Log in to OpenSubtitles if your account access requires it. Verify write access beside the video and choose an archive entry when requested; an existing subtitle is not overwritten.

### Missing duration, resolution or codecs

Wait for scanning/probing to finish. Confirm FFprobe is bundled or run yarn ffprobe:fetch for source development. Check THEAMA_FFPROBE is not none or an invalid path. Retry the source scan and inspect logs; an unreadable, unsupported or damaged file may still fail probing.

### Download completes but does not appear in Library

Check the actual qBittorrent save path. Map movie/series destinations to existing library sources, or add the actual completed folder as a source and scan it. Theama cannot scan a remote client’s unrelated local path. Verify the downloaded item contains video files and is not excluded.

### Keys or player preferences missing after restore

Database backups exclude provider secrets and desktop/profile preferences. Re-enter the keys and client login in Settings, install/select the player, and verify the restored folders. Never attempt to recover credentials by posting the secrets folder to a support issue.

### Setup status unavailable or progress not remembered

Refresh status after connecting the backend. Configured subtitle credentials need Test in this session to establish current access. An unknown VPN state is not protection confirmation. If local profile storage is blocked, progress is kept only in memory for the session; configuration saved through the existing forms still uses its normal storage.

<a id="review"></a>

## Final review and verification

You can finish now even if some features are skipped. The checklist continues to show incomplete and unavailable items in Setup Guide.

1. Confirm the backend is Connected, at least one accessible source is added, and a local video opens in your chosen player.
2. For each optional feature you enabled, check its own verification: a correct TMDB poster/match, a subtitle-provider test and downloaded subtitle, or a connected client plus a working release search.
3. Create a library backup once you have useful watched history or manual identifications. Note that secrets and media files need separate care.
4. Choose Finish setup to return to the library. Reopen Settings → Setup Guide to review every instruction, refresh statuses, configure skipped features, or restart the wizard without deleting existing settings.

Configured means the feature has suitable configuration/current evidence; Needs attention flags an error or inaccessible resource. Not configured means nothing is set up. Skipped records your choice only while the feature remains unset. Status unavailable means the app cannot currently establish its condition. It never means that a connection succeeded.
